title: A phone left at Grind & Gossip lights up: 'Reward if found: C$100.' Jojo's on break.

outcomes.text: You hand it to Jojo, who labels it 'PHONE (NOT YOURS) (JOANNE?)' and drops it in the lost-and-found mug.

later.text: Remember the phone at Grind & Gossip? Its owner left you a prepaid latte. Jojo spelled your name wrong on it, on purpose.

outcomes.text: Mom answers, then the owner does. You meet on 30th Avenue. She cries a little and hands you C$100 in a birthday card.

options.label: Read the group chat first
options.get: Prime tea for the Tea app

outcomes.text: The group chat is planning a breakup at a taverna. You know everything now, and you hand the phone to Jojo like an angel.
Juicy chat, then you hand it over. Clout in your pocket, some guilt in the other.

later.text: Remember the phone at Grind & Gossip? Its owner saw her chats marked 'read' while it was missing. Jojo told her who found it.

title: An envelope taped under Gus's bench in Astoria Park: C$200 and a note, 'for Marisol.'

options.label: Ask Gus who Marisol is
options.get: The story, and a warm feeling

outcomes.text: Gus knows Marisol: she walks dogs here. He tells you how he met his wife in 1987, then calls her. The envelope gets home.

later.text: Remember the envelope under Gus's bench? Marisol left you a box of her mother's pão de queijo and a thank-you on the bench.

outcomes.text: You put it back exactly how it was taped. Gus nods. You're not sure if he saw, but Gus always saw.

options.label: Take half, leave half
options.riskWhy: Gus watches that bench all day

outcomes.text: C$100 in your pocket, C$100 under the bench. A compromise nobody asked for.

later.text: Remember the envelope under Gus's bench? He told Marisol it was 'a little lighter' after you sat there. Everyone on the bench knows now.

options.label: Take the envelope
options.riskWhy: Gus sees everything on that bench

outcomes.text: Envelope in your jacket. The note says 'for Marisol, love Mom.' That's going to stay with you.

later.text: Remember the envelope under Gus's bench? Gus has been telling every jogger about 'the one who took it.' He describes you very well.

title: Tariq's cart, 2 AM. He gives you change for a fifty. You paid with a twenty.

outcomes.text: Tariq laughs, takes the thirty back and says honesty at 2 AM is rarer than a parking spot on Steinway. Extra sauce.

later.text: Remember the wrong change at Tariq's cart? He told every cabbie on the block. One knocked C$20 off your ride home.

options.label: Pocket the C$30
options.riskWhy: He counts the till at 4 AM

outcomes.text: You walk off with a platter and thirty bonus dollars. The sauce tastes slightly of guilt. Still good.
Thirty dollars and a platter. Tariq waves you off with a smile that makes it worse.

later.text: Remember the wrong change at Tariq's cart? His till came up C$30 short that night. Now he 'forgets' your extra white sauce.

options.label: Fix it, pay for the next guy
options.get: A nurse off shift gets a free platter

outcomes.text: You hand the thirty back and cover the nurse behind you. She says it's the nicest thing since her shift started at 7 PM.

title: Mr. Penwright's book sale: a signed first edition priced C$2 by mistake. Collectors pay C$300.

outcomes.text: Mr. Penwright goes pale, then pink. 'The roof fund thanks you.' He forgives a late fee you didn't know you had.

later.text: Remember the C$2 first edition? It sold at auction for the roof fund. Mr. Penwright put your name on the thank-you board.

options.label: Buy it to keep
options.riskWhy: It's on your shelf, nowhere else

outcomes.text: C$2 and it's yours. It looks incredible on your shelf. Your shelf is a milk crate.
A dealer on 30th Avenue pays C$300 without blinking. Mr. Penwright's whole roof fund is C$412.

later.text: Remember flipping the C$2 first edition? Mr. Penwright saw it in a window on 30th Ave. He whispers your name now. Not kindly.

title: A sax player at the Unisphere nails a solo. Walt's tour group is filming. You got the best angle.

options.label: Post it with his name
options.get: Some clout, and a happy sax player
options.riskWhy: Credit is hard to get wrong

outcomes.text: His name's Desmond and he's played the Unisphere since it was 'only slightly rusty.' Walt adds your clip to his tour.

later.text: Remember crediting Desmond's sax solo at the Unisphere? A wedding booked him off your clip. He sent you C$40 and a voice note.

outcomes.text: 'Found this legend in Flushing 🎷.' The legend is now yours, apparently. People ask you to book him.
Your clip does numbers. Walt's tour group posts theirs too, a few hours later, with his name.

later.text: Remember the Unisphere sax clip? Walt's tour group posted theirs with Desmond's name and a comment: 'unlike some people.'

outcomes.text: You drop a twenty in his case and ask for something slow. Walt's whole tour group sways. No clip, all vibe.

title: Rev. Mercy's bake sale honor box: C$4 a slice, nobody watching, and you have exactly C$1.

options.label: Leave C$1 and an IOU
options.cost: C$1 and your name on a napkin
options.riskWhy: Your name is literally on it

outcomes.text: You write 'IOU C$3' on a napkin and sign it. The lemon pound cake is worth every cent you don't have.

later.text: Remember your napkin IOU in Rev. Mercy's honor box? She pinned it to the board: 'Honest folk eat free Friday.' You ate free Friday.

options.label: Skip the cake
options.cost: Smelling it all the way home

outcomes.text: You walk past the cake. The cake does not walk past you. You can smell lemon until 31st Street.

options.label: Take a slice, 'pay later'
options.riskWhy: Someone always sees in a chapel

outcomes.text: You take a slice and promise the box you'll be back. The box has heard that before.
A slice for the road, and a promise to pay later. The cake is perfect. The promise is not.

later.text: Remember the 'pay later' slice? Rev. Mercy mentioned, very kindly, that the box was C$4 short Tuesday. She looked right at you.

title: Engine 7's chili fundraiser: C$5 a bowl, honor jar, Captain Rosa up a ladder. You're starving and broke.

options.label: Offer to work for a bowl

outcomes.text: Captain Rosa hands you a sponge and a bowl. Hydrant the dalmatian supervises. The chili tastes like a job well done.

later.text: Remember scrubbing pots for chili at Engine 7? Captain Rosa told the whole firehouse. They waved you to the front at the block party.

outcomes.text: You eat fast and wave at the jar like it's a friend you'll call later. Captain Rosa is still up the ladder.
The chili is incredible. You tell the jar you'll be back. Captain Rosa is looking down from the ladder.

later.text: Remember the 'next time' chili at Engine 7? Captain Rosa saw from the ladder. She told the firehouse group chat, laughing. Mostly laughing.

outcomes.text: You walk on. Hydrant follows you half a block, judging. Dalmatians are very judgmental.

title: The line at Still-a-Dollar Slice is 40 deep. A guy near the front waves: 'Yo, I saved you a spot.'

options.label: Go to the back
options.get: A slice you can look at

outcomes.text: You wave him off and join the back. Arben, folding slices, gives you a nod that means 'correct.'
You slide in. Nobody says anything, because it's New York and everyone is saving it for the group chat.
You slide in. A woman behind you narrates it into her phone like a nature documentary. It gets 4,000 views.

options.label: Take it and wave in two more
options.get: Pizza fast, and two grateful friends

outcomes.text: You wave in two strangers you met eight seconds ago. Arben stops folding, points to the back, and the line applauds.
You wave in two strangers. They're grateful. You're a hero to two people and a villain to thirty-seven.

title: Bobblehead night at Meteor Park. Hector the usher can walk you past 300 people, 'friend of a friend.'

options.label: Wait like everyone else
options.get: A fair shot at a bobblehead

outcomes.text: You wait. They run out four people ahead of you. The guy who got the last one lets you hold it for a photo.
You wait an hour and get the second-to-last Meteors bobblehead. It nods at you like it knows.
Hector walks you through like a dignitary. You get a bobblehead and a lot of looks.

later.text: Remember skipping the bobblehead line? Section 7 recognized you at the next game and chanted 'LINE! CUT-TER!' for an inning.

options.label: Ask Hector to take the old-timer

outcomes.text: Hector walks the 80-year-old in the '86 jersey to the front. He salutes you from the gate. You get nothing. You feel great.

later.text: Remember the old-timer at bobblehead night? He left a signed '86 program for you with Hector: 'To the kid with manners.'

title: The Hub's new fries are soggy. The manager offers free fries for a month if you post five stars.

outcomes.text: 'Great booths, Lola is iconic, fries are a damp handshake.' The manager sulks. Three people thank you for the warning.

options.label: Five stars, free fries
options.riskWhy: People will try them because of you

outcomes.text: 'Best fries in Queens!!' The manager slides you a basket. They are soggy. You eat them anyway, because they're free.

later.text: Remember your five stars for The Hub's soggy fries? Twelve people came because of you. Lola read their replies aloud at the bar.

options.label: Tell the cook how to fix them

outcomes.text: You tell the cook: double-fry them. He squints, then tries it. 'Huh.' The manager pretends it was his idea.

later.text: Remember telling The Hub's cook to double-fry? The new fries are a hit, and the menu calls them 'the regular's fries.' That's you.
